answer: Trust propagates through bounded-length random walks on the attestation graph, so influence depends on reachable, independently supported paths rather than claimed identities. A sybil cluster may wander internally, but if its external cut is sparse, its conductance is low: few walks escape the hollow cluster. Under capped edge weights and bounded walk length, min-cut and transitivity bounds limit its aggregate voting weight; a nebula of fabricated nodes cannot gain influence merely by multiplying identities.
